The Shield. It's a cop show about a special anti-drug/anti-gang team in LA set in the early to mid-2000s. It deals with race, corruption, and police brutality. The Shield was my absolute favorite show (and probably still is), but I have to admit that Southland is probably even better. Southland is also about police in LA, but not so much corruption and police brutality. It's more a realistic depiction of what life as a cop is like. It's very realistic, or seems that way from someone with no law enforcement experience--like a dramatized version of Cops. You see the characters rolling out to call after call after call. The calls are about complaints and stupid arguments between residents. Things get a little monotonous. Then suddenly, crazy shit is going down and the characters respond. It does an amazing job of conveying the cop experience. And characters are incredibly well written. Characters are more 3-dimensional than in any show or movie I've seen.

Not surprised...VZW is notorious for their crappy approach. I wonder though if there isn't legal grounds for this since technically didn't the telco's get tons of tax payer funds to roll out fiber? Or was that just "broadband" in the general sense of the term?

Most big ISPs have received federal funds to some degree with the Connect America program. The smart states imposed regulations on how this money is spent, but in some states ISPs have a blank check with no oversight. I see the push for fiber (from ISPs) to be in the interest of ridding themselves of the regulations that copper POTS has. The root of the problem is that internet (and phone service) are essential utilities that we regulate like luxuries. There needs to be much greater consumer protection on service if we want to keep things run by private industry.
So they get federal funds plus charge crazy rates for decent broadband service? Sounds like a bit of double-dipping, no?

I agree. The ISPs stance seems to be: don't regulate us because we're a free market entity, but subsidize our networks because we're an essential utility. I believe that internet access is a utility, and should be both regulated and subsidized. Ideally I'd love to see the federal government building networks itself, and charge ISPs maintenance fees to offer service on the network. It's worked for highways. Right now our internet situation is like a bus company owning the highways. When a bus company owns the highway, there's no reason for them to let other vehicles on.

I'm digging the analogy! Great way to explain the issue.

Mostly I'm just fed up with the lack of meaningful/real competition when it comes to internet service...so when I hear of crap like this, it just makes me hate those companies all that much more.
